title: Same Words, Different Procedure: Counterfactual Transfer Tests for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills (Software and Reproducibility Artifacts)
description:
This versioned archive contains the implementation, frozen protocols, native interaction records, tests, audits, analyses, and manuscript sources for the Counterfactual Skill Transfer Test (CSTT).

CSTT is a state-matched six-condition protocol that crosses source procedural compatibility with lexical similarity and includes no-skill and binding-only controls. The frozen confirmation contains 60 zero-overlap ALFWorld targets, three open local model families, 180 paired target-model blocks, and 1,080 native episodes. Matched-far skills achieved 97.8% native success versus 10.0% for lexically near procedural lures, an 87.8-point paired gain (target-stratified 95% CI 82.8-93.3; task-clustered randomization p = 1.00e-6). Relative to binding-only, the net gain was 83.3 points with zero observed harmful discordances.

The archive includes integrity manifests and CPU-only verification scripts. Third-party ALFWorld data and model weights are not redistributed; pinned identifiers, revisions, paths, licenses, and integrity checks are provided instead.
